correctness.rationale: Invariance of the second coordinate gives the exact marginal pushforward \(y_\#\mu=(bx)_\#\mu\), hence the barycenter line and variance scaling. Invariance of the first coordinate gives \(a\mathbb E[x^2]=1-(1-b)m\). Factoring the fixed-point quadratic yields \(\operatorname{Var}(x)=(x_+-m)(m-x_-)\). Nonnegativity places the barycenter on the fixed-point segment; endpoint variance zero forces both coordinates constant and hence the corresponding fixed-point atom. Adding coordinate variances converts the scalar parabola into the Euclidean chord-product identity. The sharp upper bound is elementary and is attained by the invariant equal fixed-point mixture. The packaged checker verifies all algebra and the classical exact constants.

The complete Senti–Takahasi equilibrium-measure paper develops thermodynamic formalism, equilibrium measures, entropy, Lyapunov exponents, dimension, correlation decay, and a central limit theorem without a coordinate-moment or barycenter theorem. Classical parameter-space and periodic-point studies likewise address orbit existence, stability, symbolic dynamics, entropy, and fractal geometry. Direct and equivalent semantic searches did not locate the fixed-point-segment barycenter law, variance parabola, or Euclidean chord product for Hénon invariant measures.
residual_risks: The foundational publisher metadata resolves publication only to February 1976; no day was invented.
The Benedicks–Carleson article was compared from its journal abstract and bibliographic statement rather than a complete local full text.
The Hitzl–Zele and Cvitanović–Gunaratne–Procaccia comparisons were abstract-level rather than complete-document searches.
The accepted identity is algebraically short and an equivalent observation may exist under unindexed numerical-statistics terminology.

value.rationale: The Hénon map is a canonical two-dimensional chaotic map whose literature emphasizes fixed-point geometry, periodic points, strange attractors, and invariant measures. The accepted theorem connects those two usually separate viewpoints exactly: the fixed points determine the barycenter location and the entire total coordinate variance of every compact invariant measure through a single chord-product law. It yields sharp parameter-only variance bounds and an immediate consistency check for computed periodic, chaotic, or thermodynamic invariant measures. The fact that every invariant state has the same total variance as the two-fixed-point mixture with the same barycenter is a structural statement, not a numerical estimate or a restatement of fixed-point stability.
